ai_for_science.reason: The benchmark explicitly targets scientific software engineering, requiring agents to preserve scientific contracts such as units, coordinate systems, numerical invariants, physical assumptions, and domain-specific workflows. Its objective is to evaluate whether coding agents can resolve engineering tasks while maintaining scientific validity, which constitutes a contribution to AI for Science.

evidence.quote: SWE-bench Science: Can Coding Agents Resolve Engineering Tasks in Science?
failures in scientific code capable of compromising not only program behavior but also the evidence underlying scientific conclusions.

Scientific software is full of contracts that ordinary code benchmarks rarely expose: units, coordinate systems, numerical invariants, file-format semantics, physical assumptions, and domain-specific workflows.

value: Issue-driven repair of real bugs while preserving scientific semantics
Expert-exploratory autonomous reasoning about unknown scientific root causes
Engineering-integration cross-module completion of end-to-end scientific workflows

evidence.quote: Each task is organized into one of three paradigms: Issue-driven, Expert-exploratory, and Engineering-integration.

Issue-driven tasks focus on repairing known defects; Expert-exploratory tasks focus on autonomously reasoning about unknown root causes in scientific scenarios; Engineering-integration tasks focus on understanding architecture across files and connecting a complete multi-module capability chain.

raw_materials.value: Real issues, pull requests, commit records, and related literature from candidate open-source scientific-computing repositories; source-code snapshots; scientific context; public tests.

evidence.quote: 1. Source Sampling and Screening. We collect real issues, pull requests (PRs), commit records, and related literature from candidate open-source scientific-computing repositories.

value: Class-specific task re-design for Issue-driven, Expert-exploratory, and Engineering-integration paradigms

evidence.quote: All raw tasks are first generated according to a unified and auditable four-stage construction process.
1. Source Sampling and Screening. ... 2. Snapshot Freezing and Reproduction. ... 3. Public-Material Abstraction and Information Isolation. ... 4. Hidden Oracle and Counter-Calibration.
Raw tasks are further re-designed according to their fit with the three task paradigms.

ground_truth.value: Reference and alternative-valid patches, private tests, contract labels, scientific-rationale and localization support blocks, expected files, source and difficulty metadata.

evidence.quote: Evaluator-only fields include private tests, contract labels, reference and alternative-valid patches, scientific-rationale and localization support blocks, expected files, source and difficulty metadata, contamination tier, and post-hoc annotations.

evaluation.value: Patch submission into clean evaluator container with public and private tests; metrics include PublicScore, PrivateScore, Fail2Pass, Pass2Pass, and Pass@1 (exact private-test success).

evidence.quote: Private tests are mounted only after patch submission in a separate evaluator container.

For each task–attempt, PublicScore is the mean score across all applicable public test cases, and PrivateScore is the corresponding mean across private test cases. Fail2Pass is the fraction of previously failing private tests that pass after the repair, while Pass2Pass is the fraction of previously passing private tests that remain passing; Pass@1 is a binary exact-private-success measure that equals 1 only when every applicable private test passes.
